authority: CTO Round 200 ratification of CEO Round 199 proposal. Article XXXVII (Future-Novelty Test) is hereby RATIFIED as a constitutional amendment, effective Round 200.
constitutional_basis: Article VII — never weaken the verifier to rescue a claim
Article XIX — never optimize for the gate
Article XXVIII — no silent semantic promotion

the_article.article_text:
Before a candidate may advance beyond novelty level 2 (NOVELTY_SURVIVES_CURRENT_SEARCH), it must pass the FUTURE-NOVELTY TEST: 'Could a well-funded 2028 competitor plausibly build this by combining technologies that already exist in 2026?' If YES, the candidate is INVENTIVE-STEP THREATENED and may not advance to level 3 (INVENTIVE_STEP_SURVIVES) unless it demonstrates a missing capability that requires a new scientific/causal insight, not merely integration of today's components.
The test is applied as follows:
1. Enumerate the enabling components of the candidate (sensors, algorithms, data sources, models, control architectures).
2. For each component, determine: does this component exist in 2026? (Yes/No/Converging)
3. If ALL components exist or are converging in 2026: the candidate is FUTURE-NOVELTY THREATENED. It may still advance if it demonstrates a NEW DECISION CAPABILITY (a new question the clinician can answer) that is not merely the sum of its components.
4. If ANY component requires a new scientific/causal insight that does not exist in 2026: the candidate is FUTURE-NOVELTY ELIGIBLE.
5. The test is ADVERSARIAL: the coder must construct the strongest 2028-competitor build scenario before assigning novelty level 3+.
This article extends CONVERGING_TECHNOLOGY_NOT_WHITE_SPACE (Round 194) from a static 2026 obviousness test to a dynamic 2028 competitor prediction.
the_article.the_temporal_extension: CONVERGING_TECHNOLOGY_NOT_WHITE_SPACE (Round 194) asked a STATIC question: are the enabling components of this candidate visible in the 2026 literature? If yes, the candidate could not claim white space, because its ingredients were already on the table. That test contained a loophole: a candidate whose components all existed could still argue 'but nobody has COMBINED them yet,' allowing combination-of-known-parts to masquerade as invention. Article XXXVII closes this loophole by converting the static 2026 existence check into a DYNAMIC 2028 feasibility prediction. The question is no longer 'do the parts exist today?' but 'could a well-funded adversary assemble these parts into this candidate within two years?' Because the answer must be constructed ADVERSARIALLY (Step 5, applying Article XXXII's strongest-alternative mandate across time), the coder cannot hide behind 'nobody has done it yet': if a plausible 2028 team COULD do it, the candidate is inventive-step threatened even if no one HAS done it in 2026. The only surviving position is a component or insight that does NOT exist in 2026 and would still have to be discovered in 2028 — genuine new scientific/causal knowledge, not integration. In short: Round 194 froze the obviousness judgment at the moment of observation; Article XXXVII projects it forward through the eyes of the strongest future competitor.

the_relationship_to_existing_rules.extends_CONVERGING_TECHNOLOGY_NOT_WHITE_: Article XXXVII SUBSUMES AND EXTENDS Round 194. Round 194 established the principle: convergence of existing technologies is not white space. Article XXXVII turns that principle into a mandatory, mechanically enforced gate with (a) a defined five-step procedure (component enumeration, per-component 2026 existence assessment with citations, threat classification, eligibility determination, adversarial 2028 build scenario), (b) a fixed enforcement point (between novelty level 2 and level 3), and (c) a required artifact field (`future_novelty_test`) in every candidate assessment claiming level 3+. Round 194 remains in force as the underlying doctrine; Article XXXVII adds the temporal dimension (static 2026 existence -> dynamic 2028 competitor feasibility) and the adversarial discipline (the coder must BUILD the strongest competitor scenario, not merely note that components exist). A candidate that passes Round 194's static check may still fail Article XXXVII if convergence is predictable by 2028; a candidate that fails Round 194 automatically fails Article XXXVII.
the_relationship_to_existing_rules.extends_SUCCESSOR_REQUIRED: SUCCESSOR_REQUIRED_WHEN_MARGINAL_NOVELTY_REMAINS_LOW (Round 188) is the REMEDIAL rule: when a candidate is discovered to carry only marginal novelty, it must be closed and replaced by a successor with genuinely higher novelty. Its cost was demonstrated through Round 199: H4-V2 (R199-C1) and H5-V2 (R199-C2) absorbed full evaluation cycles before being CLOSED as disguised predecessors. Article XXXVII is the PREVENTIVE counterpart: it intercepts marginal-novelty candidates at the level-2-to-3 boundary, BEFORE further investment, by demanding proof that a 2028 competitor could not trivially rebuild the candidate from 2026 parts. Where SUCCESSOR_REQUIRED asks 'is what we built novel enough to keep?', Article XXXVII asks 'should this have been allowed to advance this far at all?'. Both rules remain in force: Article XXXVII filters advancement; SUCCESSOR_REQUIRED governs closure-and-replacement for anything that slips through.
the_relationship_to_existing_rules.informs_NOVELTY_CONFIDENCE_LEVELS: The novelty confidence ladder gains a hard, evidence-backed gate between level 2 (NOVELTY_SURVIVES_CURRENT_SEARCH) and level 3 (INVENTIVE_STEP_SURVIVES). Assignment of level 3+ now REQUIRES a completed `future_novelty_test` record containing: component enumeration, per-component 2026 existence verdicts with citations, the adversarially constructed 2028-competitor build scenario, identification of the missing scientific/causal/architectural insight (if any), and a PASS/MARGINAL_PASS/FAIL verdict. Verdict semantics: FAIL bars level 3 outright (candidate remains at level 2 pending successor); MARGINAL_PASS permits level 3 ONLY when the record articulates the NEW DECISION CAPABILITY or CAUSAL/ARCHITECTURAL INSIGHT that is not the sum of the components (as with R199-C3's recoverability-as-distinct-decision-variable and R199-C4's discrete model-failure declaration architecture); PASS permits level 3 directly. Levels 1 and 2 are unaffected. Retroactive scope: any candidate currently held at level 3+ without a recorded future_novelty_test must be re-assessed under Article XXXVII before any further advancement or portfolio entry.

the_test_procedure.step_1: Enumerate the enabling components of the candidate (sensors, algorithms, data sources, models, control architectures).
the_test_procedure.step_2: For each component, determine: does this component exist in 2026? (Yes/No/Converging). Cite evidence.
the_test_procedure.step_3: If ALL components exist or are converging in 2026: the candidate is FUTURE-NOVELTY THREATENED. It may still advance if it demonstrates a NEW DECISION CAPABILITY that is not merely the sum of its components.
the_test_procedure.step_4: If ANY component requires a new scientific/causal insight that does not exist in 2026: the candidate is FUTURE-NOVELTY ELIGIBLE.
the_test_procedure.step_5: The test is ADVERSARIAL: the coder must construct the strongest 2028-competitor build scenario before assigning novelty level 3+.

the_mechanical_enforcement.gate_position: Between novelty level 2 (NOVELTY_SURVIVES_CURRENT_SEARCH) and novelty level 3 (INVENTIVE_STEP_SURVIVES). A candidate may not be assigned novelty level 3+ without passing the Future-Novelty Test.
the_mechanical_enforcement.required_artifact: Each candidate advancing to level 3+ must include a `future_novelty_test` field in its assessment JSON with: (a) component enumeration, (b) 2026 existence assessment per component, (c) 2028-competitor build scenario, (d) the new scientific/causal insight required (if any), (e) PASS/MARGINAL_PASS/FAIL verdict.
the_mechanical_enforcement.ci_check: The pre-commit hook (per Article XXXVI enforcement pattern) should verify the `future_novelty_test` field exists for any candidate with novelty_confidence_level >= 3. Phase 1: manual check. Phase 2: pre-commit hook. Phase 3: CI.

This is a new CAUSAL INSIGHT, not merely integration.

components_2026: safe RL with OOD detection (OGSRL NeurIPS)
application_to_round_199_candidates.competitor_2028_build_scenario: A 2028 competitor could combine closed-loop shunt + industrial mismatch detection + safe RL. HOWEVER, the integrated architecture — discrete model-failure DECLARATION (vs continuous updating) + AUTOMATIC device-initiated re-identification (vs clinician-triggered) + SAFE POLICY SWITCHING during re-identification (vs mere abstention) — is NOT in the 2026 literature. The competitor would need to discover this architectural insight.
application_to_round_199_candidates.new_scientific_insight_required: The ARCHITECTURAL INSIGHT that model failure should be a DISCRETE EVENT triggering automatic re-identification and safe policy switching, rather than continuous gradual model updating (iLet) or mere abstention (H6/safe RL). This is a new ARCHITECTURAL INSIGHT, not merely integration.

the_constitutional_amendment_record.the_seven_conditions_analogy: Just as Article XXXVI (Experiment Validity Gate, Round 160) made experiment validity mechanical rather than procedural, Article XXXVII makes future-novelty assessment mechanical rather than procedural. Both articles add a gate that prevents epistemic inflation.
